category: Electrochemistry: Current Distribution Features, Kinetics & Couplings
description: Shared nodes of the Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Current Distribution interfaces (Electrochemistry, Battery Design, Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer, Corrosion and Electrodeposition Modules): electrode kinetics, surfaces and porous electrodes, thin layers, applied currents and potentials, load cycling, initialization study, heating couplings and result variables. Type strings come from COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models.

tools.name: Electrolyte Charge Conservation Model (Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck)
tools.description: Interface-level choice in Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck (tcd) of how ionic charge and mass transport are coupled. Electroneutrality eliminates one species from the electroneutrality condition; Water-based with electroneutrality adds water auto-ionization with H+ and OH- transport; Supporting electrolyte assumes the charge is carried by ions of constant concentration; Electroanalysis sets the electrolyte potential to zero (no ohmic drop, used by the Electroanalysis entry); Poisson solves the Poisson equation without electroneutrality for diffuse double layers.
tools.usage: Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck > Electrolyte Charge Conservation; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("tcd").prop("SpeciesProperties").set("ChargeTransportModel", "Electroneutrality")

parameters.name: ChargeTransportModel
parameters.description: Electroneutrality, WaterBased, SupportingElectrolyte, Electroanalysis or Poisson.

parameters.name: FromElectroneutrality
parameters.description: Index of the species computed from electroneutrality (choose an inert, abundant ion).

parameters.name: prop("TransportMechanism") Convection / Migration
parameters.description: Include convection and migration terms.

parameters.name: PhysicsVsMaterialsReferenceElectrodePotential
parameters.description: Reference electrode scale (default SHE) used when taking potentials from materials.

tools.notes: Flux and concentration conditions cannot be set for the species eliminated by electroneutrality. Electroanalysis disables features that act on the electrolyte potential.

tools.name: Electrode Kinetics Expression Types (Electrode Reaction)
tools.description: Options of the Electrode Kinetics section of Electrode Reaction and Porous Electrode Reaction nodes that define the local current density iloc from the overpotential. Butler-Volmer (exchange current density i0, anodic and cathodic transfer coefficients), Linearized Butler-Volmer for small overpotentials, Anodic or Cathodic Tafel equations (Tafel slopes), Concentration Dependent Kinetics (CO, CR factors), Fast Irreversible Electrode Reaction (transport-limited), Thermodynamic Equilibrium (primary condition), plus From material and user-defined expressions; batteries add insertion and lithium-metal kinetics. An optional limiting current density caps |iloc|.
tools.usage: Electrode Surface > Electrode Reaction > Electrode Kinetics > Kinetics expression type; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("cd").feature("es1").feature("er1").set("ElectrodeKinetics", "ButlerVolmer")

parameters.name: ElectrodeKinetics
parameters.description: ButlerVolmer, LinButlerVolmer, AnodicTafelEquation, CathodicTafelEquation, ConcentrationDependentKinetics, FastIrreversibleElectrodeReaction, ThermodynamicEquilibrium (plus LithiumInsertion, LithiumMetal, InsertionReaction in battery interfaces).

parameters.name: i0Type / i0 / i0_ref
parameters.description: Exchange current density: user value, FromNernstEquation, MassActionLaw or LumpedMultistep (tertiary).

parameters.name: alphaa, alphac
parameters.description: Anodic and cathodic transfer coefficients.

parameters.name: Aa, Ac
parameters.description: Anodic and cathodic Tafel slopes (Ac negative).

parameters.name: Limiting current density ilim
parameters.description: Optional upper bound for mass-transport limitations.

parameters.name: clim
parameters.description: Linearization limit for concentration dependence at low concentration.

tools.notes: Prefer Nernst Equation + Butler-Volmer over Concentration Dependent Kinetics for thermodynamic consistency. Linearized Butler-Volmer is useful for troubleshooting convergence. No Marcus-type kinetics option is listed in the local 6.4 documentation.

tools.name: Equilibrium Potential and Nernst Equation (Electrode Reaction)
tools.description: Equilibrium Potential section of Electrode Reaction nodes: Eeq can come from the material (for example battery electrode OCV curves), from the Nernst Equation relative to a reference equilibrium potential Eeq,ref, or from a user expression. In the tertiary interface the concentration dependence follows the stoichiometric coefficients and reference concentrations; elsewhere it uses the reduced/oxidized species expressions CR and CO. The Heat of Reaction section supplies dEeq/dT or a thermoneutral voltage for reversible heat.
tools.usage: Electrode Reaction > Equilibrium Potential; Java: feature("er1").set("Eeq_ref", "0.34[V]"); set("EeqrefType", "userdef")

parameters.name: Eeq / EeqrefType / Eeq_ref
parameters.description: Equilibrium potential source and reference value (builtin or user defined).

parameters.name: CR, CO
parameters.description: Reduced/oxidized species expressions for non-tertiary interfaces.

parameters.name: cref
parameters.description: Reference concentrations (tertiary interface).

parameters.name: dEeqdT / Etherm
parameters.description: Temperature derivative or thermoneutral voltage for the reversible heat source.

tools.notes: Overpotential eta = phis - phil - Eeq (minus film losses). The interface setting Physics vs. Materials Reference Electrode Potential converts material data to the chosen reference scale.

tools.name: Film Resistance (Electrode Surface)
tools.description: Electrode Surface setting that adds an ohmic potential drop across a resistive film between electrode and electrolyte, for example insulating deposits, passive layers or coatings. The film resistance is given directly as a surface resistance or computed from an initial thickness, the thickness change from deposition/dissolution, and the film conductivity. An extra dependent variable for the film potential drop enters the overpotentials of all reactions on that surface.
tools.usage: Electrode Surface (or Internal/Thin Electrode Surface) > Film Resistance; Java: feature("es1").set("FilmResistanceType", "SurfaceResistance")

parameters.name: FilmResistanceType
parameters.description: NoFilmResistance, SurfaceResistance or ThicknessAndConductivity.

parameters.name: Rf
parameters.description: Surface resistance (ohm*m^2).

parameters.name: sf0, sigmaf
parameters.description: Initial film thickness and film conductivity.

tools.notes: Useful for coating resistance in cathodic protection and electrophoretic painting-like problems.

tools.name: Double-Layer Capacitance (Electrode Surface)
tools.description: Subnode of Electrode Surface or Internal Electrode Surface that adds the nonfaradaic current from charging the electric double layer, proportional to the double-layer capacitance Cdl and the time derivative of the potential difference. It is needed for transient techniques such as EIS, current interrupt and cyclic voltammetry and improves numerical stability with load steps. In tertiary interfaces the stoichiometric coefficients define which species exchange with the double layer.
tools.usage: Electrode Surface > Double-Layer Capacitance (dlc1); Java type: "DoubleLayerCapacitance"

parameters.name: Cdl
parameters.description: Double-layer capacitance (F/m^2).

parameters.name: nm, Vi0
parameters.description: Electrons and stoichiometric coefficients for mass exchange (tertiary interfaces).

tools.notes: Not available in Primary Current Distribution. The double-layer current is zero in stationary studies.

tools.name: Porous Matrix Double-Layer Capacitance (Porous Electrode)
tools.description: Porous Electrode subnode adding a volumetric nonfaradaic current from double-layer charging at the matrix-electrolyte interface. The source is proportional to Cdl and the double-layer area per volume, which can be given directly or derived from particle size. It is essential for supercapacitors, battery impedance and fuel-cell EIS.
tools.usage: Porous Electrode > Porous Matrix Double-Layer Capacitance (pdl1); Java type: "PorousMatrixDoubleLayerCapacitance"

parameters.name: Cdl
parameters.description: Double-layer capacitance per interface area (F/m^2).

parameters.name: ActiveSpecificSurfaceAreaType / av_dl / rp
parameters.description: Double-layer area per volume, user defined or ParticleBasedArea from particle radius.

parameters.name: nm, stoichiometric coefficients
parameters.description: Species exchange for tertiary/battery interfaces.

tools.notes: Not available for Primary Current Distribution.

tools.name: Porous Electrode Reaction (Current Distribution)
tools.description: Subnode of Porous Electrode (or Highly Conductive Porous Electrode) defining a charge-transfer reaction distributed through the porous volume. The kinetics, equilibrium potential and stoichiometry are set as in Electrode Reaction, and the Active specific surface area av multiplies iloc to give a volumetric current source iv (A/m^3). Several subnodes model parallel or competing reactions.
tools.usage: Porous Electrode > Porous Electrode Reaction (per1); Java type: "PorousElectrodeReaction"

parameters.name: av
parameters.description: Active specific surface area (m^2/m^3); particle-based in battery interfaces.

parameters.name: ElectrodeKinetics, i0, alphaa, alphac
parameters.description: Kinetics as for Electrode Reaction.

parameters.name: Eeq
parameters.description: Equilibrium potential (material, Nernst or user defined).

tools.notes: Result variables: <tag>.iv_per1 and the feature-scoped <tag>.pce1.per1.iv; total <tag>.ivtot.

tools.name: Highly Conductive Porous Electrode
tools.description: Domain node for porous electrodes whose electronic conductivity is so high that the electrode phase potential is uniform. Only the pore-electrolyte charge (and species) balance is solved in the domain, and the electrode phase potential is set by a condition such as electric potential, electrode potential, total current or load cycle, as for Electrode Surface. It reduces the problem size for metal foams, meshes and anodes.
tools.usage: Current Distribution interface > Highly Conductive Porous Electrode (hcpce1); Java type: "HighlyConductivePorousElectrode"

parameters.name: Electrode phase potential condition
parameters.description: Electric potential, Electrode potential, Total current, Average current density, Load cycle.

parameters.name: epsl, correction models
parameters.description: Electrolyte volume fraction and effective transport corrections.

parameters.name: Porous Electrode Reaction subnodes
parameters.description: Distributed reactions.

tools.example:
Application Library: Corrosion_Module (cp_with_anode_deformation uses it for porous anodes) and Electrodeposition_Module cu_trench_deposition_ls.
model.component("comp1").physics("tcd").create("hcpce1", "HighlyConductivePorousElectrode", 2);
tools.notes: Harmonic Perturbation settings are available for impedance studies.

tools.name: Current Conductor (Electrochemistry)
tools.description: Domain node for regions that conduct current only in the electron-conducting phase, such as solid metal electrodes, current collectors, feeders, gas diffusion layers and backings. Ohm's law with the electric conductivity sigma_s defines the current, with optional linear temperature dependence of resistivity.
tools.usage: Current Distribution / Battery interface > Current Conductor (cc1); Java type: "CurrentConductor"

parameters.name: sigma
parameters.description: Electric conductivity tensor (from material or user defined).

parameters.name: rho0, alpha, Tref
parameters.description: Linearized resistivity parameters.

tools.notes: Use Internal Electrode Surface on boundaries between a Current Conductor and an Electrolyte domain.

tools.name: Internal Electrode Surface
tools.description: Boundary node for the electrode-electrolyte interface between an explicitly modelled electrode domain (Current Conductor) and an electrolyte domain, or on exterior boundaries of porous electrodes. It hosts Electrode Reaction and Double-Layer Capacitance subnodes and supports film resistance and dissolving-depositing species. Examples are lithium-metal anodes, internal short circuits and current-collector dissolution.
tools.usage: Current Distribution / Battery interface > Internal Electrode Surface (bei1); Java type: "InternalElectrodeSurface"

parameters.name: Film Resistance
parameters.description: Optional ohmic film.

parameters.name: Dissolving-depositing species
parameters.description: Species with molar mass and density for growth/dissolution.

parameters.name: Electrode Reaction subnodes
parameters.description: Kinetics at the interface.

tools.notes: If the electrode conductivity is high, replace the electrode domain with an Electrode Surface boundary condition.

tools.name: Perforated Electrode Surface
tools.description: Electrode Surface variant applied on interior boundaries of electrolyte domains to model a thin, highly conductive perforated (mesh) electrode immersed in electrolyte. Apart from the interior-boundary selection it is identical to Electrode Surface, including electrode phase potential conditions and load cycles.
tools.usage: Current Distribution interface > Perforated Electrode Surface (interior electrolyte boundaries)

parameters.name: Electrode phase potential condition
parameters.description: As in Electrode Surface.

parameters.name: Electrode Reaction / Double-Layer Capacitance
parameters.description: Subnodes.

tools.example:
1. Draw an interior boundary representing a mesh cathode inside an electrolysis cell.
2. Add Perforated Electrode Surface with an Electrode Reaction for hydrogen evolution.
3. Set Electric potential = 0 V and solve the Secondary Current Distribution.
tools.notes: For non-perforated thin sheets with different reactions on each side use Thin Electrode Surface.

tools.name: Thin Electrode Surface
tools.description: Interior-boundary node for an infinitely thin electrode fully immersed in electrolyte, avoiding meshing of thin metal sheets in 3D. The electrolyte potential becomes a slit variable with separate up and down values, and reactions can be active on both sides or only one; film resistance can be set per side. Typical for electrodeposition or corrosion on sheet metal.
tools.usage: Current Distribution interface > Thin Electrode Surface (tes1); Java type: "ThinElectrodeSurface"

parameters.name: SideSelection
parameters.description: Both, Up or Down side active.

parameters.name: FilmResistanceType / FilmLocation
parameters.description: Film on both or one side (Rf_up, Rf_down).

parameters.name: Species, Ms, rhos
parameters.description: Dissolving-depositing species with molar mass and density.

parameters.name: BoundaryCondition
parameters.description: ElectricPotential, TotalCurrent, LoadCycle, CyclicVoltammetry, etc.

tools.notes: Side-specific variables carry u/d suffixes.

tools.name: Thin Electrolyte Layer
tools.description: Interior-boundary node representing a thin insulating or resistive sheet within an electrolyte, such as shields, separators or membranes, without meshing it. For the resistive option the surface resistance is given directly or from thickness and conductivity. An advanced option slits the electrode potential in porous electrodes.
tools.usage: Current Distribution interface > Thin Electrolyte Layer (tel1); Java type: "ThinElectrolyteLayer"

parameters.name: ThinLayerType
parameters.description: Insulating or Resistive.

parameters.name: LayerSpecification
parameters.description: SurfaceResistance (Rs) or ThicknessAndConductivity (dl, sigmal).

parameters.name: SlitElectricPotential
parameters.description: Also insulate the electrode phase in porous electrodes.

tools.notes: Thin Electrode Layer is the counterpart inside electrode domains (contact resistance).

tools.name: Thin Electrode Layer
tools.description: Interior-boundary node representing a thin insulating or resistive sheet inside an electrode domain, for example a contact resistance between two electronic conductors. Resistance is set directly or from thickness and conductivity, and an advanced option slits the electrolyte potential in porous electrodes.
tools.usage: Current Distribution interface > Thin Electrode Layer (interior boundaries of electrode domains)

parameters.name: Layer type
parameters.description: Insulating or Resistive.

parameters.name: Surface resistance / Thickness and conductivity
parameters.description: Resistance specification.

tools.example:
1. Split a current collector into two domains at a welded tab.
2. Add Thin Electrode Layer on the shared boundary with Surface resistance = 1e-6[ohm*m^2].
3. Evaluate the voltage drop across the tab.
tools.notes: Available in Secondary and Tertiary Current Distribution and battery interfaces.

tools.name: Edge Electrode
tools.description: 3D edge feature that models thin wires, pipes and rods as lumped 1D electrodes on edges inside or adjacent to electrolyte domains. Tangential conduction follows Ohm's law, a fixed potential, a floating potential, an external short to another electrode, or a connection point. It holds Electrode Reaction, Double-Layer Capacitance, External Current Source, Electric Ground, Electric Potential and Electrode Current subnodes.
tools.usage: Current Distribution / Cathodic Protection interface > Edge Electrode (edge1) > Electrode Reaction; Java type: "EdgeElectrode" (reaction subnode "EdgeElectrodeReaction")

parameters.name: Edge electrode radius
parameters.description: Radius of the wire or pipe.

parameters.name: Electric potential condition
parameters.description: Ohm's law (conductivity), fixed, floating, external short or connection point.

parameters.name: External Current Source
parameters.description: Line current source q (A/m) along the edge.

tools.notes: Film resistance is available on the edge electrode surface.

tools.name: Electrode-Electrolyte Boundary Interface
tools.description: Advanced boundary node for an electrochemical interface on an outer boundary of an electrode domain when the electrolyte is not modelled explicitly. The electrolyte potential is set directly or by a total current or average current density condition, and Electrode Reaction and Double-Layer Capacitance subnodes define the kinetics. Available in Secondary and Tertiary Current Distribution interfaces.
tools.usage: Show Advanced Physics Options > Current Distribution interface > Electrode > Electrode-Electrolyte Boundary Interface

parameters.name: Boundary condition
parameters.description: Electrolyte potential, Total current or Average current density.

parameters.name: Electrode Reaction subnodes
parameters.description: Kinetics referring to the electrolyte potential.

tools.example:
1. Model only a thin resistive wafer seed layer as the electrode domain.
2. Apply Electrode-Electrolyte Boundary Interface on its top surface with electrolyte potential 0 V.
3. Add an Electrode Reaction for copper deposition and solve for the terminal effect.
tools.notes: Hidden by default; enable Advanced Physics Options to see it.

tools.name: Electrolyte Current / Electrolyte Current Density
tools.description: Boundary conditions on electrolyte boundaries. Electrolyte Current sets the total inward current or average current density while keeping a uniform electrolyte potential on the boundary (an extra global unknown). Electrolyte Current Density prescribes the local normal current density distribution and can carry a Harmonic Perturbation for impedance studies.
tools.usage: Current Distribution interface > Electrolyte Current (ic1) / Electrolyte Current Density; Java type: "ElectrolyteCurrent"

parameters.name: IonicCurrentType
parameters.description: TotalCurrent (Itl) or AverageCurrentDensity (Ial).

parameters.name: phil0init
parameters.description: Initial guess for the electrolyte potential.

parameters.name: inl
parameters.description: Normal current density for Electrolyte Current Density.

tools.notes: In 1D and 2D the total current uses the cross-sectional area or out-of-plane thickness of the interface.

tools.name: Electrode Current Density (Electrochemistry)
tools.description: Boundary condition prescribing the normal electronic current density on an exterior boundary of an electrode or porous electrode domain, for example a current collector tab or the outer face of a 1D battery. It can host a Harmonic Perturbation for impedance studies; in 2D/3D Electrode Current is preferred when a uniform potential is expected.
tools.usage: Current Distribution / Battery interface > Electrode Current Density (ecd1); Java type: "ElectrodeNormalCurrentDensity"

parameters.name: nis
parameters.description: Normal electrode current density (A/m^2); positive into the domain.

tools.notes: Property nis_type = NormalElectrodeCurrentDensity selects the normal-current form; isbnd gives a current density vector instead.

tools.name: Electrode Power
tools.description: Boundary condition that sets the electrical power drawn from or supplied to a cell at an external electrode boundary, as total power or average power density, with an optional contact resistance. The potential adjusts to deliver the requested power. Used for constant-power discharge of batteries and capacitors.
tools.usage: Current Distribution / Battery interface > Electrode Power (epow1); Java type: "ElectrodePower"

parameters.name: ElectrodePowerType
parameters.description: TotalPower (Pts) or AveragePowerDensity (Pas).

parameters.name: phisgrnd
parameters.description: Ground potential reference for the power computation.

parameters.name: phis0init
parameters.description: Initial guess for the electrode potential.

parameters.name: IncludeContactResistance, Rc
parameters.description: Optional contact resistance.

tools.notes: Combine with a stop condition on cell voltage to end the discharge.

tools.name: Harmonic Perturbation (Electrochemistry, EIS)
tools.description: Subnode (or section) that applies a small harmonic amplitude to Electric Potential, Electrolyte Potential, Electrode Current Density, Electrolyte Current Density or Electrode Surface conditions. It is active only in Frequency-Domain Perturbation study steps, as used by the AC Impedance studies, giving impedance spectra (Nyquist and Bode plots) around the stationary or time-dependent operating point.
tools.usage: Right-click Electric Potential / Electrode Current > Harmonic Perturbation (hp1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("liion").feature("pot1").create("hp1", "HarmonicPerturbation", 0)

parameters.name: deltaphis
parameters.description: Perturbation amplitude of the electric potential (e.g. 5 mV).

parameters.name: deltaphisext / deltaItot / deltaIavg
parameters.description: Amplitudes in Electrode Surface for potential, total current or average current density conditions.

tools.notes: Impedance Z = delta_phi/delta_I is evaluated with lindev() of potential and current variables; the AC Impedance study templates create Nyquist/Bode plots automatically.

tools.name: External Short (Electrochemistry)
tools.description: Boundary condition that connects two electrodes through an external connector with resistance R. The selected boundary is kept at a constant potential and its integrated current follows Ohm's law with respect to the potential of the connected electrode chosen in the Connected Potential list. Used for galvanic couples, sacrificial anodes, stray current and external short-circuit tests.
tools.usage: Current Distribution interface > External Short (or Electrode Surface > Boundary condition = External short); Cathodic Protection edge variant Java type: "EdgeExternalShort"

parameters.name: R
parameters.description: External resistance (ohm).

parameters.name: Connected potential
parameters.description: Potential of the other electrode (phis,there).

tools.example:
Application Library: Corrosion_Module pipeline_corrosion_protection_iccp (edge external short between anode and pipe).
1. Add External Short on the anode boundary.
2. Select the cathode potential in Connected potential and set R = 0.1[ohm].
tools.notes: Electrode Surface also offers External short as a boundary condition option (BoundaryCondition = ExternalShort).

tools.name: Reference Electrode (Electrochemistry)
tools.description: Point feature placed in an electrolyte domain that defines a global reference potential from the local electrolyte potential plus the equilibrium potential of a chosen reference reaction. Electrode Potential conditions and result variables (electrode potential vs. reference) can then refer to it, mimicking a physical reference electrode such as Ag/AgCl or Li/Li+.
tools.usage: Current Distribution / Battery interface > Reference Electrode (refel1, point); Java type: "ReferenceElectrode"

parameters.name: Eeq
parameters.description: Equilibrium potential of the reference reaction (from material, Nernst or user defined).

tools.notes: Electric Reference Potential is the analogue defined in an electrode domain point. In Cathodic Protection the point variant is ReferenceElectrodePoint.

tools.name: Electric Reference Potential
tools.description: Point feature applicable to electrode domains that defines a global electric reference potential equal to the electric potential at that point. Electrode Potential boundary conditions can then set an electrode potential relative to this reference.
tools.usage: Current Distribution interface > Electric Reference Potential (point in an electrode domain)

parameters.name: Point selection
parameters.description: Point inside or on an electrode domain.

tools.example:
1. Add Electric Reference Potential at the tip of a current feeder.
2. In Electrode Potential choose this reference and set 0.5 V.
tools.notes: Use Reference Electrode for references located in the electrolyte.

tools.name: Load Cycle (Electrochemistry)
tools.description: Generic load-cycling boundary condition for time-dependent simulations built from Current, Voltage, Rest (and in battery interfaces C Rate, Power, Subloop) child nodes. Switching between steps is driven by elapsed time, voltage or current limits, or user conditions via internal events, and cycling can stop after a number of cycles. It is a boundary node on electrode exterior boundaries or a child of Electrode Surface / Highly Conductive Porous Electrode when their condition is Load cycle.
tools.usage: Current Distribution / Battery interface > Load Cycle (lc1) > Current / Voltage / Rest; Java type: "LoadCycle"

parameters.name: LoadType
parameters.description: Galvanostatic, Potentiostatic or PotentiostaticAndGalvanostatic.

parameters.name: useTimeConditionsOnly
parameters.description: Use only elapsed-time continuation conditions.

parameters.name: CyclingStopCondition, N_cycles_max
parameters.description: Stop after a maximum number of cycles or other condition.

parameters.name: phis0init / E_app_init
parameters.description: Initial potential guess.

parameters.name: AddSolverStopConditions
parameters.description: Add stop conditions to the solver automatically.

tools.notes: Apply the Load Cycle on the positive side of the cell. The Potentiostatic and galvanostatic option adds an extra unknown and may be less stable.

tools.name: Current / Voltage / Rest (Load Cycle subnodes)
tools.description: Child nodes of Load Cycle that define one step of the cycle: Current sets a current (A), Voltage sets a cell voltage (V), Rest sets zero current. The set value can be a constant, a function of the elapsed step time, or a step sequence table; continuation conditions (elapsed time, maximum/minimum voltage or current, user expression) decide when to proceed to the next step.
tools.usage: Load Cycle > Current (curr1) / Voltage / Rest (rest1); Java types: "Current", "Voltage", "Rest"

parameters.name: InputType
parameters.description: Value, Function or Step sequence.

parameters.name: setVal / setFun
parameters.description: Set current or voltage value or function.

parameters.name: TimeCondition, tmax
parameters.description: Elapsed-time continuation condition.

parameters.name: MaxVoltageCondition, Emax / MinVoltageCondition, Emin
parameters.description: Voltage-limit continuation conditions.

parameters.name: UserDefinedCondition
parameters.description: Custom logical condition.

tools.notes: Galvanostatic load cycles allow only Current, Rest and Subloop; potentiostatic only Voltage and Subloop.

tools.name: Circuit Terminal (Electrochemistry)
tools.description: Boundary node that couples an electrochemical cell boundary to an External I vs. U element in the Electrical Circuit interface, so the cell can be driven by or embedded in a lumped circuit (loads, protection circuits, equivalent circuits). Requires an AC/DC Module or Battery Design Module license.
tools.usage: Current Distribution / Battery interface > Circuit Terminal; Electrical Circuit > External I vs. U referencing the terminal

parameters.name: Terminal
parameters.description: Name used by the External I vs. U circuit element.

tools.example:
1. Add Circuit Terminal on the positive current collector of a Secondary Current Distribution cell.
2. In Electrical Circuit add External I vs. U and select the terminal.
3. Add a Resistor load and solve.
Related Application Library model: Battery_Design_Module/Batteries,_General/overdischarge_protection couples a Lumped Battery to a circuit through an External I vs. U element (type ModelDeviceIV).
tools.notes: Electrode Surface also provides a Circuit terminal boundary condition option.

tools.name: Electrode / Electrolyte Current Sources (domain, line, point, symmetry axis)
tools.description: Additional source features adding current into the electron-conducting or electrolyte phase: domain Electrode/Electrolyte Current Source (A/m^3), Line Current Source on 3D edges or 2D points (A/m), Point Current Source (A), and Symmetry Axis Current Source in 2D axisymmetry. They represent wires, sacrificial feeders or unresolved electrodes.
tools.usage: Show Advanced Physics Options > Additional Sources > Electrode Current Source / Electrolyte Current Source (ics1); line/point variants on edges and points; Java type (domain electrolyte source): "ElectrolyteCurrentSource"

parameters.name: Qs / Qli
parameters.description: Volumetric electrode or electrolyte current source (A/m^3); Qli is the electrolyte source property.

parameters.name: ql,s / ql,l
parameters.description: Line current source (A/m).

parameters.name: Point current
parameters.description: Point source strength (A).

tools.notes: In localized_corrosion_ls the source Qli = i_loc*ls.delta smears the pit-surface current over the level-set interface.

tools.name: Ion-Exchange Membrane (Tertiary Current Distribution)
tools.description: Domain node for a permselective membrane with a fixed space charge added to the electroneutrality condition, transporting all interface species. Negative fixed charge gives a cation-selective and positive charge an anion-selective membrane. Donnan equilibrium boundary conditions can be applied automatically at membrane-electrolyte interfaces, with optional Donnan shift of initial values. Used for flow batteries, electrodialysis and chlor-alkali cells.
tools.usage: Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck > Ion-Exchange Membrane (iem1); Java type: "IonExchangeMembrane"

parameters.name: rhofix
parameters.description: Fixed space charge density (C/m^3), e.g. -cHm*F_const.

parameters.name: ApplyDonnanBoundaryConditions
parameters.description: Donnan equilibrium on adjacent boundaries.

parameters.name: AddDonnanShiftToInitialValues
parameters.description: Shift initial values to satisfy electroneutrality.

parameters.name: D_c, um, epsl, correction models
parameters.description: Membrane transport properties.

tools.notes: Donnan conditions are not available with the Poisson charge conservation model.

tools.name: Ion-Exchange Membrane Boundary (Tertiary Current Distribution)
tools.description: Exterior-boundary condition coupling a free electrolyte to a separately modelled ion-exchange membrane: the flux of one charge-carrying species is continuous while the electrolyte potential shifts by a specified membrane potential. Used when the membrane and free electrolyte are solved in different interfaces or with different species sets, for example in flow-battery models.
tools.usage: Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck > Ion-Exchange Membrane Boundary (iemb1); Java type: "IonExchangeMembraneBoundary"

parameters.name: Charge-carrying species
parameters.description: Species carrying the current across the boundary.

parameters.name: Membrane potential
parameters.description: Electrolyte potential on the membrane side.

tools.notes: If both sides share the same species, the Ion-Exchange Membrane domain node is usually simpler; for interior boundaries use Thin Electrolyte Layer.

tools.name: Separator (Tertiary Current Distribution)
tools.description: Domain node for electrolyte charge and mass transport in an electronically isolating porous matrix, with correction factors (for example Bruggeman) reducing diffusivities and conductivities according to volume fraction and tortuosity. Settings for diffusion and migration are as for the Electrolyte node.
tools.usage: Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck > Separator (sep1); Java type: "Separator"

parameters.name: epsl
parameters.description: Electrolyte volume fraction (porosity).

parameters.name: DiffusionCorrModel / IonicCorrModel
parameters.description: Bruggeman, tortuosity or user-defined corrections.

parameters.name: D_c, um
parameters.description: Species diffusivities and mobilities.

tools.notes: Battery interfaces have their own Separator nodes with the same Java type.

tools.name: Adsorbing-Desorbing Species and Initial Values (Electrode Surface)
tools.description: Electrode Surface section defining species that adsorb or desorb on the electrode during faradaic or nonfaradaic reactions. A density of sites and site occupancy numbers set up surface mass balances for fractional coverages theta, available as variables like tcd.theta_es1_<species> and tcd.thetafree_es1 for use in kinetics. The Initial Values for Adsorbing-Desorbing Species subnode sets the starting coverages.
tools.usage: Electrode Surface > Adsorbing-Desorbing Species table; subnode Initial Values for Adsorbing-Desorbing Species (ivads1); Java type: "InitialValuesForAdsorbingDesorbingSpecies"

parameters.name: AdsorbingDesorbingSpecies
parameters.description: Table of species with site occupancy numbers Sigma.

parameters.name: Gamma
parameters.description: Density of sites (mol/m^2).

parameters.name: Initial coverage
parameters.description: Initial fractional surface coverage of each species.

tools.notes: Surface diffusion of adsorbates requires the Surface Reactions interface.

tools.name: Dissolving-Depositing Species and Nonfaradaic Reactions (Electrode Surface)
tools.description: Electrode surfaces and porous electrodes can declare dissolving-depositing species (molar mass, density) whose surface concentration and thickness change with the electrode reactions, giving deposit thickness and electrode growth velocity for deformed-geometry models. Nonfaradaic Reactions adds chemical (non-electrochemical) rates for these species, and Initial Values for Dissolving-Depositing Species sets their starting amounts.
tools.usage: Electrode Surface / Internal Electrode Surface / Porous Electrode > Dissolving-Depositing Species; subnodes Nonfaradaic Reactions (nfr1) and Initial Values for Dissolving-Depositing Species (ivdds1); Java types: "NonFaradaicReactions", "InitialValuesForDissolvingDepositingSpecies"

parameters.name: Species, Ms, rhos
parameters.description: Dissolving-depositing species with molar mass and density.

parameters.name: SolveForDissolvingDepositingConcentrationVariable
parameters.description: Solve for the surface concentration variable.

parameters.name: R / Rad
parameters.description: Nonfaradaic reaction rates for dissolving-depositing and adsorbing species.

tools.example:
Application Library: Battery_Design_Module/Lithium-Ion_Batteries,_Aging_and_Abuse/lmo_decomposition (nonfaradaic LMO decomposition) and Batteries,_General/zn_ago_battery_1d.
model.component("comp1").physics("liion").feature("pce1").create("nfr1", "NonFaradaicReactions", 1);
tools.notes: Stoichiometric coefficients of the dissolving-depositing species in Electrode Reaction nodes define the deposition rate by Faraday's law.

tools.name: Current Distribution Initialization (study step)
tools.description: Stationary study step that solves only for the electric and electrolyte potentials (and global ODE variables) to provide consistent initial values for a following Stationary or Time Dependent step; all other variables stay at their initial values. The Primary type (default) uses equilibrium-potential constraints for the reactions, while Secondary includes kinetics and is preferable when ohmic drop is negligible (cathodic protection, mixed potential, thin resistive wafers). It is part of the Stationary with Initialization and Time-Dependent with Initialization studies.
tools.usage: Study > Current Distribution Initialization (cdi); Java: model.study("std1").create("cdi", "CurrentDistributionInitialization"); model.study("std1").feature("cdi").set("initType", "secondary")

parameters.name: initType
parameters.description: primary (default) or secondary current distribution type.

parameters.name: Physics and variables selection
parameters.description: Interfaces solved in the step (same as Stationary).

tools.notes: When several reactions share one electrode, the Equilibrium Potential Handling (Primary Condition) setting selects the first or average Eeq for the constraint.

tools.name: Electrochemical Heating (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling that adds domain and boundary heat sources in a heat transfer interface from the irreversible (Joule heating, activation losses) and reversible (entropic) heat of an electrochemistry interface, and passes the heat-transfer temperature back to the electrochemistry interface. It is the standard way to couple battery, fuel-cell or electrolysis models to thermal models.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Electrochemical Heating (ech1); Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("ech1", "ElectrochemicalHeating", 3)

parameters.name: ECHeat_physics
parameters.description: Electrochemistry interface providing heat sources (cd, liion, fc, ...).

parameters.name: Heat_physics
parameters.description: Heat transfer interface (ht).

tools.notes: Heat of reaction requires dEeq/dT or a thermoneutral voltage in the (Porous) Electrode Reaction nodes.

tools.name: Potential Coupling / Space Charge Density Coupling (multiphysics)
tools.description: Couplings used to build Nernst-Planck-Poisson type models from separate interfaces. Potential Coupling passes the potential from a source interface (such as Electrostatics) into the migration term of a chemical species transport interface; Space Charge Density Coupling computes the local space charge from species concentrations and charges and adds it to the Poisson equation of Electrostatics.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Potential Coupling (pc1) / Space Charge Density Coupling (scdc1); Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("pc1", "PotentialCoupling", 1)

parameters.name: PotentialSource_physics / PotentialDestination_physics
parameters.description: Source (es) and destination (tds) interfaces for Potential Coupling.

parameters.name: Source / Destination (Space Charge Density Coupling)
parameters.description: Species transport interface and Electrostatics interface.

tools.notes: The Tertiary Current Distribution interface with the Poisson charge conservation option is an alternative single-interface formulation.

tools.name: Electrochemistry Result Variables (phil, phis, Eeq, eta, iloc, itot, iv, nIl, nIs)
tools.description: Predefined variables of the electrochemistry interfaces for postprocessing and couplings. Potentials: phil (electrolyte), phis (electrode), <tag>.phisext, <tag>.Eeq_<er> (equilibrium) and <tag>.eta_<er> (overpotential). Currents: <tag>.iloc_<er> (local current density), <tag>.itot (sum at a surface), <tag>.iv_<per> and <tag>.ivtot (volumetric), <tag>.nIl and <tag>.nIs (normal electrolyte/electrode current densities), <tag>.IlMag and <tag>.IsMag. Total currents are obtained by integrating over electrode boundaries or domains.
tools.usage: Results > Derived Values / plots, e.g. Surface Integration of cd.iloc_er1 over an electrode; feature-scoped forms like cd.es1.er1.iloc also exist

parameters.name: <tag>
parameters.description: Interface name, e.g. cd, tcd, liion, fc.

parameters.name: <er>/<per>
parameters.description: Tag of the (Porous) Electrode Reaction node, e.g. er1, per1.

tools.notes: In 1D/2D axisymmetric enable Compute integral in revolved geometry for total currents; an Integration component coupling can define a total-current variable usable during solving.

tools.name: Solver Strategies for Current Distribution Problems
tools.description: Documented practices for converging electrochemistry models: ground one electrode to fix potential levels, use Stationary or Time-Dependent with Initialization (Current Distribution Initialization first), switch the initialization to Secondary if needed, derive initial potentials by a potential walk from the least-polarized electrode, try Linearized Butler-Volmer while troubleshooting, and refine porous-electrode meshes toward the electrolyte. For load steps use smoothed functions, add double-layer capacitance, limit the maximum time step or use Events.
tools.usage: Study settings and physics initial values; see Solving Electrochemical Models in the module User's Guides

parameters.name: Current Distribution Initialization type
parameters.description: Primary or Secondary.

parameters.name: Time stepping
parameters.description: Maximum step, Steps taken by solver = Strict/Intermediate.

parameters.name: Kinetics
parameters.description: Temporary Linearized Butler-Volmer.

tools.example:
1. Replace a Stationary study by Stationary with Initialization.
2. If the second step fails, set cdi initType = secondary and review phil/phis initial values.
3. For pulse loads set Time Dependent > Maximum step = pulse length/5.
tools.notes: Double-layer capacitance also regularizes discontinuous current steps.
